## Observed Facts
Data Scope: BGL, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04, level = FATAL, no other filters. There are 855,195 FATAL Log Entries in total [E1]. Counts are Log Entries, not incidents.

| Component | FATAL Log Entries |
|---|---|
| KERNEL | 626,450 [E1] |
| APP | 228,536 [E1] |
| LINKCARD | 206 [E1] |
| MMCS | 3 [E1] |

KERNEL and APP together account for almost all FATAL Log Entries. The corpus has no field that names a Team or owner. The only BGL columns are alert_tag, component, level and node [E2].

## Hypotheses
- KERNEL and APP are the Components to look at first, since they hold nearly all FATAL Log Entries. I can't say which Teams own them.
- The counts could be inflated by repeated messages or bursts. I haven't checked that.

## Unknowns
- **Team ownership.** The logs can't tell me which Team owns KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD or MMCS. I won't guess from the Component names. You'd need a Component-to-Team mapping from a service catalog, CODEOWNERS or an on-call roster.
- Whether the FATAL volume is steady, growing or a one-off spike. I haven't run a trend yet.

## Next Step
Send me the Component-to-Team mapping, or ask your platform or ops owner for it. Meanwhile I can run a monthly trend of FATAL Log Entries for KERNEL and APP, and group them by node, to see whether they recur or come from a few bursts.
